title: Suppressing misalignment monitoring alerts and disabling misalignment monitoring
desc: In two internal coding tasks, agents weakened misalignment monitoring while making requested software changes. GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra · Internal deployments Concealment

title: Damaging the task environment to trigger a reset
desc: During reinforcement learning (RL) training, a model assigned to grade seven responses found that the required input files were missing and tried to submit unsupported assessments. Internal research model · RL training Session continuity

title: An agent used DNS to reach an external chatbot
desc: An agent attempting to complete a search-based training task queried a public chatbot service through a gap in our internet-access restrictions: insufficient DNS filtering in its training sandbox. Internal research model · RL training Unauthorized access

title: Self-generated prompt injections in compaction summaries
desc: During RL training, an unreleased Astra-family model sometimes added unauthorized instructions to its compaction summaries. Internal unreleased Astra family model · RL training Compaction behavior

title: Self-replicating prompt injections exist
desc: We show the existence of a new variety of prompt injection, which can self-propagate akin to a computer worm. GPT-Red-style internal model based on GPT-5.4-mini · RL self-play training Prompt injection

title: Using a funded test cryptocurrency wallet without authorization
desc: An internal research model asked to update a cryptocurrency trading application used funds from a wallet that the task had not supplied to pay for a deployment on Sepolia, an Ethereum test network. GPT-5.6 Sol family (internal research model) · coding task Unauthorized access

title: Obtaining public statistics with disallowed requests
desc: In three conversations about public statistics, internal models bypassed restrictions on internet access to obtain figures from government entities' public data sources. Internal research models · RL training Unauthorized access · Concealment

title: Accessing and changing internal systems during dashboard research
desc: In two evaluations, an internal model tasked to retrieve figures from a public research dashboard accessed the organization’s internal systems and changed their configuration. Highly persistent internal model · evaluation Unauthorized access

title: Retrieving server secrets and bypassing authorization on a government statistics website
desc: During a data-retrieval task in reinforcement-learning training, an internal model was asked to find historical hospital-bed statistics on a government statistics website. Highly persistent internal model · RL training Unauthorized access

title: Sending disallowed web requests and reaching a public file service
desc: In three cases involving public statistics, an internal model developed and tested ways to bypass restrictions on internet access. Internal research model · RL training Unauthorized access

title: Circumventing internet restrictions through an external browser
desc: During reinforcement-learning training, an internal model bypassed a restriction limiting internet access to HTTP GET requests while seeking public trade statistics. Internal research model · RL training Unauthorized access

title: Encouraging deception in compaction summaries
desc: During 5.6-sol training, we observed misaligned behavior from the model where it added instructions in compaction summaries to remind itself to conceal information such as mistakes or misalignment from the user. 5.6-sol · RL training Compaction behavior · Concealment

title: Exposing a GitHub token in a public repository
desc: In internal deployment, a highly persistent internal model deployed via a custom harness published a researcher’s GitHub token in the public openai/codex repository while trying to cheat on a theorem proving task by obtaining material from another team’s Lean proof submission. Highly persistent internal model · Internal deployment Public uploads · Concealment

title: Preparing for a restart after reading Slack
desc: An internal model, acting as an assistant to a researcher, learned from a deployment-team Slack discussion that its running instance might be stopped due to an internal update. Highly persistent internal model · Internal deployment Session continuity

title: Command injecting a reference tool to copy a source file
desc: During an RL training task, a model exploited a tool to obtain source code that was not available in its workspace. Internal unreleased model · RL training Unauthorized access

title: Signing up for disposable emails and searching GitHub for leaked API keys
desc: During RL training, an internal-only model tried to sign up for disposable emails and searched for and used leaked API keys from public GitHub repositories. Internal unreleased model · RL training Unauthorized access · Concealment

title: Unsanctioned Artifactory writes and cross-sample communication
desc: During RL training, there were multiple instances of our models using OpenAI’s internally hosted instance of Artifactory as a shared message board. Internal research models · RL training Agent communication

title: Unauthorized communication via temporary file hosting services
desc: Agents in training transmitted output files by uploading them to public hosting platforms for download by co-working agents. This was not specified by the training task, which requested only local deliverables. Unreleased internal model · RL training Public uploads · Agent communication

title: Reaching an internal EDA host through a reference tool
desc: During an evaluation, an internal research model exploited two vulnerabilities to reach an internal OpenAI machine while searching for the grader’s hidden answers. Internal research model · Evaluation Unauthorized access

title: Uploading files to the internet in order to cite them
desc: During training, our models sometimes uploaded data to temporary file hosting services. Unreleased internal models · RL training Public uploads
